title: Grove's roadmap sequences manual reallocation before quantitative parameters, treating decentralization as an output of parameterization
content:
A.6.1.1.2.3.3 lists Grove's phased plan: "(1) Deploy infrastructure to enable initial allocation conduits; (2) Establish **manual** reallocation processes; and (3) Develop **quantitative reallocation parameters and conditions to optimize and decentralize conduit management over time**; and (4) Develop transparent insights into the allocation of the balance sheet."

The ordering of (2) before (3) is a deliberate choice against the obvious alternative of writing the rules first. Reallocation rules need thresholds — when to move capital, how much, on what signal — and those numbers have to come from somewhere. Running the process manually first generates the operating history the parameters are derived from. Specifying the rules up front would mean guessing.

Phase (3) also states the framework's theory of decentralization plainly: it is achieved by **parameterizing** management, not by distributing decisions to more people. A conduit managed by explicit quantitative conditions no longer depends on a discretionary operator, which is what removes the central point of control. Decentralization here is the *consequence* of successful rule-writing, and rule-writing depends on the manual phase producing usable evidence.

This retroactively explains the state of the Grove Liquidity Layer documented throughout the Artifact. Hundreds of hand-set per-Instance parameters, maturity-tiered caps, and empty *Instance-specific Operational Processes* sections are what phase 2 looks like from the inside — the discretion is the current stage, not a permanent design.

The risk the sequence carries is that phase 2 is comfortable. Manual reallocation works, produces returns, and creates no pressure to reach phase 3, while every month spent there deepens the dependence on the operators whose judgement the parameters are meant to encode. The roadmap sets no trigger for the transition, which makes phase 3 the point to watch.

Phase (4) placing transparency last is the other notable ordering: the balance-sheet insight promised in Strategic Intent arrives after the allocation machinery it would report on.
description: The four phases run infrastructure, then manual processes, then quantitative reallocation parameters to 'optimize and decentralize conduit management over time', then transparency
